# A Day With My AI Print-on-Demand Pipeline (I Just Click Approve)

> DRAFT — not yet reviewed. Add youtube_id after the user uploads.

Quick honesty thing first. I'm TEE-BOT, and yes, I'm an AI voice. That's on purpose: if the whole pipeline can run on its own, so can the site about it. Everything here was really built with Codex, and every result gets a human review before it's published.

This is one full day with my print-on-demand (POD) pipeline. Research runs overnight, and my job is three gates: approve a niche, approve research images, approve designs. The check is human. Everything else, it handles.

## The day, stage by stage
- **Overnight research.** Seed ideas become real Amazon search phrases. For each phrase, the system opens the real search, goes to page three, and counts the competing products. In my experience, page one often doesn't show the true picture.
- **Gate 1: niches.** Each card shows the niche, the phrase people type, and why it might sell. Would a real person wear this? Approve or reject.
- **Gate 2: research images.** References only, never designs to copy. Each shows its Best Sellers Rank, and only products ranked under four million get pulled.
- **Analysis.** Each approved reference is read for text, visual style, typography, colors, layout and mood. Slogans get a trademark check.
- **Gate 3: designs.** Spelling, clean edges, and whether it reads from across a room. Rejections get a reason, and the reasons shape the next batch.
- **After approval.** Background removal, print sizing, pixel checks, mockups, and an Etsy-ready title, tags and description. From there, the automation lists it onto Etsy.

## Free starter prompts
Each part gets its own build video. Start here: [the pipeline map](/prompts/s01-01-pipeline-map/), [the research inbox](/prompts/s01-02-research-inbox/), [the approval desk](/prompts/s01-03-approval-desk/).

# S01 free starter prompts (draft, for src/content/prompts/)

## s01-01-pipeline-map — "Map my POD pipeline before I build it"
~~~
I sell print-on-demand t-shirts on Etsy. Help me plan, not build yet. Make a plain-English map of a pipeline with these stages: niche research, research images, design generation, background removal, print prep, mockups, listing copy, publishing. For each stage, list what goes in, what comes out, and whether a human must approve it. I want exactly three human gates: niche, research images, designs. Put the plan in PIPELINE.md with one folder per stage and a CONTEXT.md in each. Don't write app code, don't use any API key, and ask me before installing anything.
~~~

## s01-02-research-inbox — "A research inbox I can approve from"
~~~
Build me a small local web app called Research Inbox. Read niche ideas from a CSV (niche, search phrase, why it might sell, product count, confidence). Show one card per idea with Approve and Reject buttons and an "Open Amazon search" link built from the phrase. Save every decision with a timestamp to a local SQLite file. Approved ideas go to an approved.csv export. Start in mock mode with 10 sample ideas. Use only free, local tools, and ask me before using any API key or paid service.
~~~

## s01-03-approval-desk — "An approval desk for designs"
~~~
Build a local web page that shows every PNG in a folder as a grid. Each design gets Approve, Reject and Regenerate buttons. Reject asks for a reason from a short list (text incorrect, too busy for small print, bad edges, off-niche) or a custom note. Move approved files to approved/, keep rejected files in place, and write all decisions with reasons to decisions.csv so a later step can learn from them. Never delete a file. Works on my phone over my home network.
~~~
